key_insight: Adding a monolayer graphene contact to AlInN/Si solar cells improves current collection and overall efficiency without significantly changing open-circuit voltage.
engineering_relevance: Graphene can serve as a low-temperature transparent conductive contact that boosts performance in nitride-based photovoltaic devices on silicon.
method: Built AlxIn1-xN solar cells on p-type Si(100) with an a-Si buffer layer
Tested three Al compositions: x = 0.22, 0.35, and 0.43
Transferred a monolayer graphene film onto the front surface as a semitransparent contact
evidence_signal: Under illuminated and dark measurements, graphene-enabled devices showed higher short-circuit current density, fill factor, and power conversion efficiency across all compositions, while Voc stayed nearly unchanged.
watch_item: The abstract does not report long-term stability, contact uniformity, or scalability of the graphene transfer process.
paper_title: Enhancement of nitride-based solar cells using graphene as transparent contact layer
